science_vegetable: Fe-Co-Cr-Ni-Mn High-Entropy Alloy lattice stabilization against galvanic corrosion induced by twin-sun eddy currents and copper flange couplings.
text:
For a man who could persuade impossible metals to sing, the ordinary, stubborn silence of rust was a particular insult. Silas knelt in the damp twilight of the arboretum, watching a slow, rhythmic drip from the main irrigation line. The pipe was a masterpiece—a Fe-Co-Cr-Ni-Mn high-entropy alloy forged to withstand the twin suns' magnetic shear. Yet someone had patched a cracked valve with a basic copper flange. The resulting galvanic corrosion, accelerated by the planet's atmospheric eddy currents, was chewing through the iron lattice.

He dragged a thumb across the oxidized blush, the structural failure registering as a personal insult. He had designed the resonant shield plating to deflect cosmic radiation, yet a single stubborn drip and a bad plumbing decision were currently defeating him. He needed to arrest the thermodynamic decay, but doing it properly meant dismantling the entire line, leaving the fragile Pearlescent Mycena lucentipes in the dark for hours.

His jaw tightened. A familiar paralysis threatened to lock his joints. If he couldn't fix it perfectly, perhaps he shouldn't touch it at all. He reached for his multi-tool, his breath shallow, the urge to obsessively catalog every micro-fracture overwhelming his tactical sense. But the drip accelerated, hitting a broad leaf with a mocking, rhythmic smack.

Silas snapped back. Precision was a luxury; the crops needed water now. He snatched a heavy iron wrench from his belt and brought it down hard against the flange, aiming for the oxidized buildup rather than the joint itself.

Clang. The vibration hummed up his arm. The dripping paused, the particulates temporarily shocked back into alignment. He stared at the bruised metal, a bitter scowl on his face.

Footsteps crunched on the gravel behind him, heavy and fast. "If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Hector's voice boomed, bouncing off the arboretum walls. The Stormbreaker walked into the soft bioluminescent glow, tossing a heavy spool of conductive cabling from hand to hand.

"I am applying kinetic shock to reseat oxidized particulates," Silas muttered, refusing to look up from the ugly dent he had just made. "It is a temporary measure."

"It's hitting a pipe with a wrench," Hector corrected cheerfully, squatting down beside him to inspect the handiwork. "And it worked. Therefore, you are a genius. Now come on, I need your eyes on the primary lightning rod coupling before the next supercell hits."
